title: "Errata"
subtitle: "On Schwarz and Coppock (2022), *The Journal of Politics* 84(2)"
format:
  pdf:
    output-file: schwarz_coppock_2022_errata.pdf
    geometry: margin=1.25in
    fontsize: 11pt
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{caption}
        \captionsetup{labelformat=empty}
        \usepackage{float}
        \floatplacement{table}{H}
        \floatplacement{figure}{H}
---

The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/schwarz_coppock_2022> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168421>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

studies <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_study_level.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
counts <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_in_text_numbers.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
f3_pooled <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_3_meta_summary.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

trim <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_2_trim_sensitivity.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE)
trim_archive <- trim |> filter(str_starts(rule, "Archive"))
trim_text <- trim |> filter(str_starts(rule, "Text"))
f3_cells <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_3_plotted_estimates.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
sen2_female <- f3_cells |> filter(study_id == "sen_2", panel == "Female respondents")
sen2_male <- f3_cells |> filter(study_id == "sen_2", panel == "Male respondents")
n_bib_keys <- n_distinct(studies$bib_entry)
n_measured <- sum(studies$digitally_measured == 1)
n_measured_papers <- n_distinct(studies$bib_entry[studies$digitally_measured == 1])

share_positive <- mean(studies$estimate > 0)
n_positive <- sum(studies$estimate > 0)
n_negative <- sum(studies$estimate < 0)
n_zero <- sum(studies$estimate == 0)
n_resp_gender <- f3_pooled$n_studies[f3_pooled$resp_female == "Female respondents"]

# Any significance rule is a threshold on the ratio of an estimate to its standard error,
# and both counts rise as that threshold is relaxed. Tightening it until only 23 positive
# estimates survive, and loosening it until 11 negative ones do, brackets what any rule can
# reach.
z <- abs(studies$estimate / studies$std.error)
threshold_23_positive <- sort(z[studies$estimate > 0], decreasing = TRUE)[23]
negatives_there <- sum(studies$estimate < 0 & z >= threshold_23_positive)
threshold_11_negative <- sort(z[studies$estimate < 0], decreasing = TRUE)[11]
positives_there <- sum(studies$estimate > 0 & z >= threshold_11_negative)

appendix_cells <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_a2_a45_plotted_estimates.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
# One per-study figure per study in the meta-analysis, so the count of distinct figures is
# how many rows Table A.1 should have.
n_ta1_expected <- n_distinct(appendix_cells$figure_number)
n_costa <- sum(appendix_cells$figure_number == 18)
n_appendix_cells <- 2 * sum(appendix_cells$figure_number != 18)

# R11. Entry 2 changes which estimates count as significant, so every sentence that rests on
# a significance verdict is re-asked under the corrected rule rather than left to the reader.
# The article asserts a verdict for three studies one at a time, all on published p. 661, and
# each is recomputed here from the deposit.
named_verdicts <- studies |>
  filter(study_id %in% c("ono_yamada_1", "kage_1", "horiuchi_1")) |>
  mutate(verdict = case_when(
    conf.high < 0 ~ "negative and significant",
    conf.low > 0 ~ "positive and significant",
    estimate == 0 ~ "exactly zero",
    TRUE ~ "not significant"))
verdict_of <- function(id) named_verdicts$verdict[named_verdicts$study_id == id]
n_named_holding <- sum(named_verdicts$verdict %in%
                         c("negative and significant", "positive and significant",
                           "exactly zero"))

# Simas and Murdoch (2019) is the study entry 5 finds missing from Table A.1. Whether that
# omission reaches Figure A.1, which the appendix defines as the distribution of the CATEs
# "conditional on each of the attributes listed in Table A.1", is a question about how much
# of that distribution the unlisted study accounts for.
n_all_cates <- nrow(appendix_cells)
n_simas_cates <- sum(appendix_cells$study_id == "simas_1")

# The prose spells small counts out, so the spine's row count has to be spelled too.
spelled <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  if (n <= length(words)) words[n] else as.character(n)
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and the document below is rendered
# from it. The same rows are written out as errata_entries.csv at the foot of this file, so
# any other rendering of these corrections (the README's counts, a remastered edition) reads
# them rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy that can drift out of agreement.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, and is the only markup a field carries. Each renderer
# resolves it its own way: bold here, \was{} in an edition. Everything else in a field is
# literal text.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
# A renumber must never change which claim_ids an entry claims.
#
# Entry 1 corrects the same overstatement in two places, so its published and corrected
# fields each hold two passages joined by a blank line, and its location holds both pages
# joined by "; ". Its emitter splits them back apart. It is one error and stays one row.
#
# `form` is a renderer's choice of treatment: "full" where the published and corrected
# fields are whole sentences that need setting as blocks, "brief" where the entry is a token
# replacement.
# `claim_ids` names the ground truth rows the entry corrects, semicolon separated, and it is
# what makes "has this finding been published?" a query over the corpus rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where the entry has no ground truth row: a reference list is not
# an extraction claim, and neither is a figure that failed to print. A row an entry discusses
# but declines to correct is not listed either, which is why entry 2 carries only the count of
# negative estimates and not the two significance counts it leaves unresolved. Every id listed
# here is checked against the ground truth by ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R, which refuses
# to finish on a dangling one.
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. Each value comes from the same expression
# that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks
# that each one is still inside the span it belongs to. An entry that corrects nothing (a
# note, or any class other than quantity) carries NA, and so does a quantity entry whose
# claim is not a number printed in the corrected sentence.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The share of studies with a positive effect is overstated, in two places",
  "p. 659; p. 664",
  paste(
    "Across the 67 studies we summarize, [[three-fourths]] find a positive effect of being described as a woman.",
    "We observe considerable study-to-study variation, although [[more than three-fourths]] of the studies show a positive effect.",
    sep = "\n\n"),
  str_glue(
    "Across the 67 studies we summarize, [[{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * share_positive)}]] find a positive effect of being described as a woman.",
    "\n\n",
    "We observe considerable study-to-study variation, although [[{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * share_positive)}]] of the studies show a positive effect."),
  str_glue(
    "Of the 67 study-level estimates, {n_positive} are positive, {n_negative} are negative ",
    "and {n_zero} is exactly zero. The positive share is ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * share_positive)} per cent, which is below three-fourths rather ",
    "than above it. The claim the two sentences make is unaffected: positive effects are the ",
    "large majority."),
  "text_prop_positive", sprintf("%.4f", share_positive),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The counts of negative and of significant estimates",
  "p. 661",
  "We see a very consistent pattern in favor of women candidates on average: 47 estimates are positive ([[23]] significant) and [[18]] are negative ([[11]] significant).",
  str_glue(
    "We see a very consistent pattern in favor of women candidates on average: 47 estimates ",
    "are positive ([[{counts$n_pos_sig_ci}]] significant) and [[{n_negative}]] are negative ",
    "([[{counts$n_neg_sig_ci}]] significant)."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited estimates divide into {n_positive} positive, {n_negative} negative and ",
    "{n_zero} exactly zero, which is the only division summing to 67. The published 47 plus ",
    "18 sums to 65.",
    "\n\n",
    "The corrected counts of significant estimates are those of the confidence interval rule ",
    "the deposited script itself applies, which gives {counts$n_pos_sig_ci} and ",
    "{counts$n_neg_sig_ci}. The published 23 and 11 correspond to no significance rule the ",
    "deposited estimates support, and not merely to a rule with a different threshold: both ",
    "counts rise as a threshold is relaxed, so no threshold can produce 23 and 11 at once. ",
    "Tightening the threshold until only 23 positive estimates remain significant leaves ",
    "{negatives_there} negative ones; loosening it until 11 negative estimates are ",
    "significant leaves {positives_there} positive ones. A test of p below 0.05 gives ",
    "{counts$n_pos_sig_p05} and {counts$n_neg_sig_p05}, and cannot be what was done in any ",
    "case, because {counts$n_missing_p} of the 67 studies carry no p-value. What procedure ",
    "produced the published pair is therefore unknown; the correction states what the ",
    "deposited rule gives.",
    "\n\n",
    "The direction of the correction favours the article's own claim: more positive estimates ",
    "reach significance than were reported, and fewer negative ones.",
    "\n\n",
    "A count of significant estimates is the warrant for the sentences that follow it, so ",
    "those were re-asked under the corrected rule. The article asserts a significance verdict ",
    "for three studies one at a time, all on published p. 661, and all three keep the verdict ",
    "it gives them: Ono and Yamada is {verdict_of('ono_yamada_1')}, Kage, Rosenbluth, and ",
    "Tanaka is {verdict_of('kage_1')}, and Horiuchi, Smith, and Yamamoto is ",
    "{verdict_of('horiuchi_1')}. The same paragraph names five further contexts as showing ",
    "negative effects and claims significance for none of them, and the deposit gives a ",
    "negative estimate in every one. No sentence in the article changes."),
  "text_n_pos_and_sig_ci_rule;text_n_negative;text_n_neg_and_sig_ci_rule", str_glue("{counts$n_pos_sig_ci};{n_negative};{counts$n_neg_sig_ci}"),

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  str_glue("Figure 3 covers {n_resp_gender} experiments, not 36"),
  "p. 663",
  "Figure 3 shows the CATEs of candidate gender, conditional on respondent gender, for the [[36]] experiments where we were able to identify respondent gender.",
  str_glue("Figure 3 shows the CATEs of candidate gender, conditional on respondent gender, for the [[{n_resp_gender}]] experiments where we were able to identify respondent gender."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited respondent-gender file carries {n_resp_gender} studies, and the published ",
    "figure itself draws {n_resp_gender} rows in each of its two panels. Figure 3 is correct ",
    "as printed and is not reproduced here; only the sentence describing it miscounts. ",
    "Nothing plotted is affected and neither pooled estimate moves."),
  "figure_3_n_studies_in_text", as.character(n_resp_gender),

  4, "float", "pipeline", "full",
  "Appendix Figure A.18 prints none of its estimates",
  "app. p. 15",
  str_glue(
    "Figure A.18, Costa (2020), USA - Lucid, is the one study in the appendix whose ",
    "randomized attribute levels are whole tweets. At the width the appendix uses, those row ",
    "labels push the plotting panel, the points, the confidence intervals, the estimate ",
    "labels and the horizontal axis off the right edge of the page. What is printed is a ",
    "column of truncated sentences, an axis title cut off after four letters, and [[no ",
    "data]]. None of the {n_costa} conditional effects the figure is drawn from appears on ",
    "the page."),
  paste(
    "Nothing is wrong with the estimates themselves; they are in the deposited archive and",
    "are unchanged. [[The figure as it should have appeared]]:"),
  str_glue(
    "The appendix promises this figure in terms: it closes its introduction by saying that ",
    "in the remainder \"we show the study-by-study estimates that make up Figure A.1\". For ",
    "Costa (2020) it shows none of the {n_costa}, which is the one place in the appendix ",
    "where that sentence does not hold. Figure A.1 itself is unaffected, since it is drawn ",
    "from the estimates rather than from these figures."),
  "", NA_character_,

  5, "float", "pipeline", "brief",
  "Appendix Table A.1 omits one of the studies it summarizes",
  "app. p. A.1",
  "Table A.1 lists [[43]] studies.",
  str_glue("Table A.1 should list [[{n_ta1_expected}]] studies."),
  str_glue(
    "The appendix carries {n_ta1_expected} per-study CATE figures, A.2 through A.45, one for ",
    "each study in the meta-analysis. Simas and Murdoch (2019) is plotted at Figure A.44 and ",
    "has no row in Table A.1, so the table describes 43 of the {n_ta1_expected}. The study is ",
    "present in the deposited data and in every pooled estimate; only the summary table ",
    "omits it.",
    "\n\n",
    "The omission is not confined to the table. The appendix introduces Figure A.1 as the ",
    "distribution of the CATEs \"conditional on each of the attributes listed in Table A.1\", ",
    "so the table is where a reader learns what that figure covers, and the unlisted study ",
    "contributes {n_simas_cates} of the figure's {n_all_cates} conditional effects. Two ",
    "estimates in {n_all_cates} cannot move the distribution, so the appendix's takeaway from ",
    "Figure A.1 stands as written. What the missing row costs is the account of one study's ",
    "attributes, which is the whole of what Table A.1 exists to give."),
  # The ground truth keys this claim as table_a1_n_studies_listed; published_claims.csv keys
  # the same claim as "table_a1 :: n_studies_listed". claim_ids points at the ground truth.
  "table_a1_n_studies_listed", NA_character_,

  6, "label", "reading", "full",
  "Three figure captions key panel letters the authors' own figures do not print",
  "p. 663; p. 664; p. 664",
  paste(
    "Figure 2. Conditional average effect of candidate gender, conditional on [[candidate race: A, black candidate; B, white candidate]]",
    "Figure 3. Conditional average treatment effects of candidate gender by [[respondent gender: A, female respondents; B, male respondents]]",
    "Figure 4. Conditional average treatment effects of candidate gender by [[respondent partisanship: A, Democratic respondents; B, Independent respondents; C, Republican respondents.]]",
    sep = "\n\n"),
  paste(
    "Figure 2. Conditional average effect of candidate gender, conditional on [[candidate race]]",

  NA_character_,

  7, "typography", "reading", "brief",

  8, "typography", "reading", "brief",

    "The deposited study-level file marks {n_measured} experiments from {n_measured_papers} papers ",
    "as having had their estimates measured from a picture, in a free-text note field. The ",
    "appendix says nine experiments in seven papers. Whether the appendix's nine leaves out one ",
    "of the marked {n_measured}, or the note field marks one the authors did not count, cannot be ",
    "settled from free text, so no corrected pair is set. The validation exercise that follows ",
    "the sentence is a test of the measurement method on one study and does not depend on the ",
    "count: no conclusion of the paper changes, and the {n_measured} marked estimates are in the ",
    "pooled results either way."),
  "", NA_character_,

  # Entry 15 is a note and not a correction: the page prints the earlier revision of one
  # study's estimates and the deposited conditional-effects file holds a later one, so which
  # value is the published figure's to carry is not a matter of replacing a token.
  # README.qmd 309.
  15, "float", "pipeline", "note",
  "Two cells of Figure 3 print an earlier revision of one study's estimates",
  "p. 663, Figure 3",
  paste(
    "Female respondents: Sen (2017), USA, SSI 2: [[6.0]] (2.2)",
    "Male respondents: Sen (2017), USA, SSI 2: [[0.5]] (2.0)",
    sep = "\n\n"),
  NA_character_,
  str_glue(
    "The figure prints 6.0 and 0.5 for Sen (2017), USA, ",
    "SSI 2, in the female and male respondent panels. The deposited respondent-gender file gives ",
    "{sen2_female$se_entry} and {sen2_male$se_entry}; the standard errors agree with the page. ",
    "The deposited study-level file carries the revised Sen SSI 2 estimate that Figure 1 ",
    "reproduces exactly, so the conditional-effects file is one revision behind the figure the ",
    "article printed. No value is set here, because replacing the two cells would present the ",
    "deposit's earlier file as the figure's intended source, which the deposit cannot show. Every ",
    "other estimate and standard error in the figure reproduces, as do both pooled estimates and ",
    "the difference between them, so no conclusion of the paper changes: two study-level points ",
    "of 74 differ by a tenth of a percentage point."),
  "", NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# values_in_spans is FALSE where the claim's scale is not the sentence's, under PROCEDURES'
# rule that corrected_values is always on the claim's scale. A method row or other id with
# no number on any scale stores NA in its position. Such an entry's note must say why.
off_claim_scale <- c(1)
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(values_in_spans = case_when(
    is.na(corrected_values) ~ NA,
    entry %in% off_claim_scale ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  ))
stopifnot(all(str_length(entries$note[!replace_na(entries$values_in_spans, TRUE)]) > 0))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where they do not. The spelled form counts as the
# numeral, since a minimal edit sets "six" and not "6".
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

spelled_numbers <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
                     "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen",
                     "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")

inside_span <- function(value, span) {
  numeral <- str_detect(span, fixed(value))
  spelled <- !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) &&
    as.numeric(value) %in% seq_along(spelled_numbers) &&
    str_detect(span, fixed(spelled_numbers[as.numeric(value)]))
  numeral || spelled
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, inside_span)) ||
      all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) inside_span(v, s)))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) inside_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note
# corrects nothing, so it carries NA even where its class is quantity, and an entry with no
# claim id has no claim to carry a value for. `unvalued` lists the quantity entries whose
# claim is not a number printed in the corrected sentence; they carry NA by decision.
# Entry 2: the ids run in the ground truth's order, not the order the counts sit in the
# sentence, so the gate accepts any value that is in some span when position does not match.
unvalued <- integer(0)
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" &
                                        !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != "" &
                                        !entries$entry %in% unvalued])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | (!is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""))
)

# form == "note" declares that the entry quotes a passage and proposes no change to it, so it
# has no corrected side. The two have to agree: a note carrying corrected text would print a
# correction this edition does not make, and a correction carrying NA would print "NA" where
# its corrected sentence belongs.
stopifnot(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note"))

# A run of entry numbers, written the way a sentence wants them. Numbered prose about the
# entries is computed rather than typed, because a hand-typed count of one's own corrections
# goes stale the moment an entry is added and looks no different when it does.
run <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(x))
  spans <- split(sort(x), cumsum(c(1, diff(sort(x)) != 1))) |>
    map_chr(~ if (length(.x) == 1) as.character(.x) else paste0(min(.x), " to ", max(.x)))
  str_flatten(spans, collapse = ", ", last = " and ")
}

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
plain <- function(x) str_remove_all(x, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]")
```

This note lists `r spelled(sum(entries$form != "note"))` corrections to "What Have We Learned about Gender from Candidate Choice Experiments? A Meta-Analysis of Sixty-Seven Factorial Survey Experiments," published in *The Journal of Politics* 84(2), doi [10.1086/716290](https://doi.org/10.1086/716290). It also carries `r spelled(sum(entries$form == "note"))` entries of a second kind, which quote a passage and propose no change to it: the Results sentence that says the trimmed estimate drops the bottom and top 5% where the code drops 3.0 and 6.0 per cent, the design sentence that counts 49 papers where the deposit has 50 bibliography keys, the appendix sentence that counts nine digitally measured experiments in seven papers where the deposit marks ten in eight, and two cells of Figure 3 that print an earlier revision of one study's estimates. **No correction and no note here changes a conclusion of the paper.** Entries `r run(entries$entry[entries$form != "note" & entries$entry != 6])` are errors in the published record, recorded because a reader who quoted it would be misled. Entry `r run(entries$entry[entries$entry == 6])` is not an error but a restoration: the journal keyed three figure captions to panel letters its own compositor added, and the authors' figures label those panels by name. Entries `r run(entries$entry[entries$form == "note"])` are neither: they are carried as the paper published them, and are described under their own heading below.

Every corrected value in entries `r run(entries$entry[entries$class %in% c("quantity", "float", "label") & entries$form != "note"])` is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/R27ULT](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/R27ULT)) at the time this document is rendered. Entries `r run(entries$entry[entries$class == "bibliographic"])` correct the reference list, which the deposit cannot speak to: entry `r entries$entry[entries$class == "bibliographic"][1]` is verified against the cited manuscript's own title page and the authoritative record at Crossref, and the two URLs against the authors' own bibliography file in the archived working folder, one of them against the article's own reference list as well. Entry `r entries$entry[entries$class == "typography"][1]` is a single letter and quotes the sentence it stands in, and entry `r entries$entry[entries$class == "typography"][2]` is a misspelled word in an appendix figure. Entry `r run(entries$entry[entries$entry == 6])` quotes the published captions themselves, which is the only thing that can settle what a caption says. The maintained code is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/schwarz_coppock_2022](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/schwarz_coppock_2022).

```{r entry-1, results="asis"}
# The one entry that quotes two passages: one row, two pages, two published-corrected pairs.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 1)
pages <- str_remove(str_split_1(e$location, "; "), "^published ")
published_passages <- str_split_1(e$published, "\n\n")
corrected_passages <- str_split_1(e$corrected, "\n\n")

cat("## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n", sep = "")
walk(seq_along(pages), function(i) {
  cat("Published, ", pages[i], ":\n\n> ", bold(published_passages[i]),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(corrected_passages[i]), "\n\n", sep = "")
})
cat(e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

# Carried, and not corrected

The `r spelled(sum(entries$form == "note"))` entries below are different in kind from the `r spelled(sum(entries$form != "note"))` corrections in this note. Each quotes a passage this edition reprints exactly as the paper published it, and proposes no change to it.

Three of them are places where the page and the deposited archive disagree and the deposit cannot say which is right: a trimming rule that the code applies differently from the text and the table label, a count of papers, and a count of digitally measured experiments. The fourth is two cells of a figure drawn from an earlier revision of one study's estimates than the deposit holds. In each case a corrected token could only be set by deciding what the authors meant, which is theirs to say, and none of the four reaches an estimate the paper rests a conclusion on. Each is recorded here because an edition that silently reproduced them would leave a reader unable to tell a faithful reprint from an uncorrected error.

```{r entries-carried, results="asis"}
# A note has no corrected side, and that absence is the whole of the form: an empty
# "Corrected:" block would read as a correction to nothing.
emit_note <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ", e$location, ":\n\n",
      str_c("> ", str_replace_all(bold(e$published), "\n\n", "\n>\n> ")), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
walk(entries$entry[entries$form == "note"], emit_note)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# states these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
# values_in_spans is written as the spine's last column, one logical per entry.
stopifnot(identical(tail(names(entries), 1), "values_in_spans"))
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
